newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary cuts 1998 govt investment target by 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hungary cuts 1998 govt investment target by 10 pct.

text.p: Hungary decided on Thursday to cut the amount to be spent on government investments in 1998 by 10 percent to 153 billion forints, government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following the cabinet meeting.
Kiss said that the differential from the originally plannned 169 billion will be spent on "soothing tension" in other areas, including the budget's of the interior and defence ministries.
The government finalised some key figures of the draft 1998 budget on Thursday.

The government also decided that total personal tax burdens should be cut by 0.2 percent in 1998, while the effectiveness of the collection of all taxes and the control on the distribution of state subsidies should be improved, Kiss said.
The government left other key 1998 budget figures, approved two weeks ago, unchanged, he added.
Hungary's 1998 gross domestic product (GDP) growth target is three to four percent, compared with two to three percent projected for this year.

The government budget deficit is seen at 4.9 percent for 1998, unchanged from the target for this year, while the current account deficit in 1998 is seen at between $2 billion and $2.5 billion, up from the $2 billion plan for 1997.
Average inflation is seen going down to 13.5 percent from about 18 percent planned for 1997, and both real wages and household consumption should increase by two percent in 1998, Kiss said.
